report.summary: Chunk defines transport sink protocol and three implementations: InMemoryTransportSink, JsonlTransportSink, CompositeTransportSink. All symbols present, claims partially checkable.

handoff.purpose: Define transport sink protocol and implementations for normalized runtime-shell records.

symbols.name: TransportSink
symbols.note: Protocol class with async publish method.

symbols.name: TransportSink.publish
symbols.note: Async method to persist or forward a TransportRecord.

symbols.name: InMemoryTransportSink
symbols.note: Sink that stores records in a list.

symbols.name: JsonlTransportSink
symbols.note: Sink that writes records to a JSONL file.

symbols.name: JsonlTransportSink.publish
symbols.note: Appends JSON line to file, creates parent dirs if needed.

symbols.name: CompositeTransportSink
symbols.note: Sink that fans out records to multiple sinks.

symbols.name: CompositeTransportSink.publish
symbols.note: Iterates over sinks and publishes to each.

claims.text: Small deterministic sink for tests and embedded consumers.
claims.why: The class is simple, stores records in a list, deterministic.

claims.text: Append-only JSONL journal preserving every normalized input/output.
claims.why: The publish method appends a JSON line to the file.

claims.text: Fan one record out to multiple sinks; failures remain visible.
claims.why: The publish method iterates over all sinks and calls publish; exceptions propagate.

claims.text: Persist or forward one lossless transport record.
claims.why: The claim refers to behavior of implementations, not defined here.

observations.what: No import of TransportRecord from .events, but used in type hints.
File path creation and locking in JsonlTransportSink are correct.
